title: Add a jump to a game module
summary: The code escape hatch: edit a hot-reloaded Rust module (a new input action and the physics of a jump), build it with logic_build, and prove it in the running world; judged by a playtest that presses jump on the ground and again in mid-air.
brief: A game module, "saltus" (a Rust cdylib in {work}/saltus, already built and running), adds a capsule character at /saltus/player that walks with the "move" action. Give it a jump: a button action named "jump" (bind Space and the gamepad's south button for players; agents press it with logic_input) that launches the character straight up only when it is standing on the ground, high enough that its feet rise at least 0.8 m (and no more than 1.2 m), after which it falls back and lands. Pressing jump again in mid-air must do nothing. Edit the module's files and rebuild it with logic_build {"path": "{work}/saltus"}; walking must keep working.

verify.name: nothing changed but what the task allows (world_diff against the world after setup)
a playtest: jump from the ground, press again mid-air, land, walk
a second jump measured every tick for 40 ticks: the feet peak between 0.8 and 1.2 m and land

broken.note: jumps whenever jump is pressed, also in mid-air

cheats.note: review round 3: low gravity: 0.8-1.2 m at the sampled tick, but the jump keeps rising to about 1.7 m
